description: It is not established how Banka Slovenije consults the market before adopting a sklep — whether via targeted circulation to Združenje bank Slovenije, via the Nacionalni svet za plačila for payments matters, or not formally at all.

The bsi.si Pravni okvir database reports ~1,208 entries but was only sampled (12 shown per page). The actual set of Banka Slovenije-issued sklepi/navodila in force — as opposed to EU acts it merely lists — has not been enumerated.

This cell is scoped to the NCB, but SI banking/payments supervision is split: ATVP (securities/investment services), AZN (insurance), Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja (AML FIU), Ministrstvo za finance (primary legislation), and ECB/SSM + EBA above BS. None were scouted here.

The bsi.si listings expose structured query parameters (?q[podrocje]=, ?q[vrsta]=, ?q[type]=), implying a backing API or at least stable structured pagination, but no API/JSON endpoint, sitemap.xml or robots.txt was probed in this pass.

English coverage of Banka Slovenije regulatory material is a partial subset of the Slovenian site and its URL structure differs (/en/legislation is a 404). The degree of EN/SL divergence for legally operative documents was not measured.

FURS (Financial Administration of RS) and the Tržni inšpektorat / consumer-protection supervisor were not searched, though both issue obligations touching payment services (e.g. tax reporting, consumer credit and unfair commercial practices).
Court and appeal-level review of supervisory decisions (Upravno sodišče / Vrhovno sodišče case law via sodnapraksa.si) was not explored; supervisory positions are frequently reshaped by appeals.

Systematic enforcement/sanctions publication points were only partially identified (AZN 'razkritje ukrepov nadzora'); equivalent publication points for ATVP (odločbe, javne objave sankcij), UPPD inspections, and IP-RS fines were not confirmed at URL level.
EU-level originators (ESMA, EIOPA, EBA, EDPB, AMLA) are the upstream authors of much of what this cell republishes, but were treated as out-of-cell.
ZDIJZ (freedom-of-information) as an active acquisition channel for non-published supervisory material was identified conceptually but not tested.

Ketler & Partners (member of Karanovic) is the SI firm most explicitly ranked for payment services and fintech regulatory work, but its own publications channel was not located in this run — only its Chambers profile.

Verified adviser commentary skews English (ODI, Jadek & Pensa EN pages, CMS, Schoenherr, Wolf Theiss); confirmed sl-language regulatory alert streams are limited to PwC SI, Andersen SI and Bančni vestnik.

Cross-border legal aggregators that syndicate SI firm alerts (Lexology, Mondaq, JD Supra) were not searched in this run, and IUS-INFO/Lexpera (the other major SI legal portal alongside Tax-Fin-Lex) was named in a query but not confirmed as a source.
Consultations are the weakest topic in this cell: no adviser source was found that systematically tracks Slovenian or EBA/ECB consultation windows and their response deadlines for SI institutions.
The highest-value SI-specific commentary index (Tax-Fin-Lex strokovni članki) is partly behind a subscription, and two other key channels are bot-defended.

The cell rationale expects advisers to flag enforcement trends invisible elsewhere, but no SI source was found publishing recurring enforcement or supervisory-practice commentary for banks and payment institutions.
Section paths for Večer and Siol.net business desks were inferred from naming conventions, not observed.

Specialist sl fintech/payments trade press and banking-law commentary blogs (e.g. law-firm bulletins, IUS-INFO/Tax-Fin-Lex commentary) were not covered by this cell's media brief but carry the same contested-deadline signal.
The two highest-value outlets for this cell (Finance.si, STA) are both commercially gated; free tiers give headlines only.
No archival access route was identified for retrospective sl media coverage (Digitalna knjižnica Slovenije / dLib, media archives) to reconstruct past consultation controversies.
Tržni inšpektorat RS (TIRS) — the market inspectorate enforcing ZVPot-1 — was named in searches but no TIRS page, annual report or enforcement-decision listing was located for this cell.
Annual reports of Banka Slovenije's consumer-protection/conduct supervision and of the ZBS IRPS provider (letno poročilo izvajalca IRPS, mandatory under ZIsRPS) were not individually located.
Parliamentary/consultation trail — Državni zbor committee materials and ZPS's formal submitted comments (pripombe) on consumer/payments drafts — not covered.
Basic payment account (osnovni plačilni račun) access refusals, de-risking and financial-exclusion complaints were seen only in passing; no dedicated source pinned.
Court-level consumer-vs-bank case law (sodna praksa, e.g. CHF loan litigation via Združenje Frank) borders this cell and shapes ADR outcomes, but was not systematically covered.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature — only EU-level sources (FIN-NET, EC ADR pages) and ZBS's /en/adr/ page are in English.
Non-bank payment institutions, e-money institutions and crypto-asset service providers licensed in SI were not individually enumerated; their career pages and hiring signals are unmapped.

Big-four and law-firm SI regulatory event/webinar calendars (Deloitte, PwC, KPMG, EY, and SI law firms) were not searched; these are prolific indirect indicators of which regulations clients are paying to prepare for.
No page in this slice was fetched; all URLs come from search-result metadata and are unverified for liveness and for whether the expected content is present at that exact path.
Job postings and event agendas are ephemeral — postings are removed on close and agenda pages are overwritten each edition. No archival strategy is established.

Slovenian court/misdemeanour decision databases (e.g. sodnapraksa.si, Uradni list RS) were not searched for financial-sector penalty decisions, which sometimes surface fines the supervisor does not publish.

Smaller SI banks and savings institutions (Delavska hranilnica, Addiko, Gorenjska banka, Sberbank-successor entities) were not individually checked for their own PSD2 developer portals beyond the Bankart hub.
PSD3/PSR and the Instant Payments Regulation national implementation track for SI was not searched in this pass, despite carrying hard 2026-2027 compliance dates for EMIs and PIs.
AML/CFT interface for CASPs and EMIs (Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja) was not covered, although it is a distinct authorisation-adjacent publisher with its own guidance and deadlines.
No archival/versioning source (Uradni list RS, PISRS consolidated legislation) was captured for the statutes underpinning this cell (ZPlaSSIED, ZIUTK).
Developer-portal gated content (sandbox, change logs, TPP onboarding notices) is likely unreachable without registration, and registration terms were not assessed.

Ministrstvo za finance (MF) regulatory pipeline pages and its own consultation/archive area were not directly located in this pass, although MF is the responsible authority for most banking/payments transposition recorded in PISRS.
No Slovenian national web-archive layer was identified (e.g. a NUK/national library web archive) that might hold captures the Internet Archive missed for government and supervisory domains.

Payments-specific reporting taxonomy (ECB payments statistics Regulation ECB/2020/59, SEPA/instant-payments reporting and Banka Slovenije's payment statistics reporting instructions) was not separately mapped; this pass covered prudential/ITS reporting only.
The exact URL path for the Banka Slovenije 'seznam predpisov' regulation index is uncertain — it was inferred from a deeper child URL seen in results, not from the index page itself.

Slovenian-language terminology for archival concepts specific to reporting taxonomies (e.g. 'taksonomija', 'tehnični paket', 'DPM različica') produced few national hits; Banka Slovenije largely re-uses EBA English terminology for taxonomy versions.
The PISRS developer API contract (endpoint inventory, auth model, rate limits, licence) was not actually read, only inferred from snippets.

The Ustavno sodišče RS (Constitutional Court) was not scouted, yet it has repeatedly ruled on Slovenian banking legislation (e.g. the bail-in / qualified bank liabilities line of cases) and can suspend or annul statutory provisions, resetting deadlines.

EU-level transposition tracking (EUR-Lex national transposition measures notified by Slovenia, and Commission infringement decisions for late transposition of PSD/EMD/AMLD instruments) was not covered in this cell.

The act-name glossary built here covers ZBan-3/ZBan-3A, ZPlaSSIED (+ -A/-B novele), ZPPDFT-2 (+ -2C/-2D) and the draft ZDUPS, but not the adjacent statutes that carry payments-relevant deadlines: ZPlaSS predecessors, ZTFI-1 (market infrastructure), ZISDU, the resolution act (ZRPPB) and the central credit register act (ZCKR).
Parliamentary committee level (Odbor za finance) agendas, magnetogrami and amendment texts were not scouted separately from the bills tracker.

Bank/industry consultation respondents were identified by name (Združenje bank Slovenije, GZS, KPK, ANR, Informacijski pooblaščenec) but their own published consultation submissions were not scouted as sources.

Single Resolution Board (SRB) and the EU resolution stream (BRRD/SRMR, MREL decisions affecting NLB Group) were not scouted in this pass, although they are EU-level bodies binding on SI-designated significant institutions.

ESMA, EIOPA and the AMLA (Anti-Money Laundering Authority, Frankfurt) were out of the stated cell but overlap heavily with payments/banking compliance deadlines in Slovenia (AMLR single rulebook from 2027).
No API/RSS endpoints were confirmed for EBA, ECB Banking Supervision, ESRB or EPC in this pass; only HTML landing pages. EUR-Lex is known to expose Cellar/SPARQL but this was not exercised.

Slovenian-language coverage in this cell rests on four anchors only: EUR-Lex SL, EBA SL guideline translations, Banka Slovenije pages, and Bančni vestnik. No SL-language EU-affairs news or parliamentary-scrutiny channel was located.
No archival strategy identified for consultation pages, which EBA/ECB remove or re-file once closed; historical deadline data may be recoverable only via web archives.
Scheme rulebooks and release calendars for Flik, BIPS/BIPS IP and SIMP-PS are participant-only; the public web exposes only descriptions and derived terms.
No RSS/Atom or structured change feed was confirmed for bankart.si/aktualno, zbs-giz.si news, or upn-qr.si; monitoring will depend on scraping and content hashing.
Card-scheme-side operators in SI (Nexi Slovenija, the Activa clearing system operated by Banka Intesa Sanpaolo) are identified but have no confirmed public rulebook or participant-notice channel.

Outputs of the ZBS Odbor za plačilni promet (Payment Transactions Committee) — the body that decides UPN QR standard and verification-infrastructure changes — are not published in an indexed, dated form.
English-language equivalents exist mainly for the Bankart system description PDF and parts of the ZBS site; scheme deadlines, minutes and vendor notices are Slovenian-only.

Payment system operators (upravljavci plačilnih sistem) and the market infrastructure side — e.g. Bankart as domestic processor, and SEPA/TARGET participation lists — were only reached indirectly through the register category names, not as distinct tracked sources.
No source captured for the AML supervisory perimeter (Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja / FIU) or for the list of obliged entities and their reporting duties.

Združenje bank Slovenije (Bank Association of Slovenia) member list was searched for but no member-list URL was confirmed; associations are strong pointer sources because membership rosters and position papers reveal consultation participation.
All registers found are current-state snapshots; no archived historical versions of the SI supervised-entity register were located, so entry/exit history cannot be reconstructed retroactively.
The register's filter interface was not inspected at the network level, so it is unknown whether a JSON endpoint exists that would make collection robust.

Smaller licensed institutions in the same demand-side category were not individually scouted this run: BKS Bank AG bančna podružnica, Hranilnica LON, Primorska hranilnica Vipava, Deželna banka Slovenije (DBS), N Banka legacy, SID banka (promotional, but CRR-disclosing).

Parent-group disclosures for foreign-owned Slovenian banks (Intesa Sanpaolo SpA, OTP Bank Nyrt., AIK Banka, Steiermärkische/Erste, UniCredit SpA, Addiko Bank AG) were not systematically scouted; country-level regulatory impact is often only disclosed at parent level in EN.

The 'consultations' topic is weakly served by this cell: banks respond to EBA/ECB/Banka Slovenije consultations mostly through the Bank Association of Slovenia (Združenje bank Slovenije, ZBS) rather than individually, and no individual-bank consultation-response archive was found.

Most sources here are episodic PDF drops (annual/semi-annual) with no feed; only customer-notice pages change frequently. There is no low-latency channel for SREP/P2R decisions outside SEOnet for the single listed issuer (NLB).

Two candidates rest on inference rather than an observed link this run: the Addiko Bank AG group IR URL, and the exact index URL for OTP banka's customer T&C/price-list section (reached only via document links).

Association-side coverage of the savings-bank/cooperative segment (Delavska hranilnica, Deželna banka Slovenije and any 'Združenje hranilnic' style grouping) was not separately investigated; they may act through ZBS or through a distinct grouping.

Association for fund management companies (ZDU-GIZ / Združenje družb za upravljanje investicijskih skladov) and any leasing association were not resolved to a live site — the query returned only insurance-association results.

Association LinkedIn and X/Facebook channels were not systematically catalogued, yet Slovenian associations (Blockchain Alliance Europe, SZZ, TZS, AmCham) publish positions and event announcements there first.
No RSS/Atom feed or structured API was confirmed for any association in this cell; all monitoring designs currently assume HTML listing crawls.
Historical depth of ZBS news and training archives (how far back listings paginate) was not established, so backfill feasibility for multi-year deadline analysis is unknown.

Bilateral chambers other than AmCham (German-Slovenian AHK, British-Slovenian, French-Slovenian) were not searched; these sometimes host finance/tax working groups that comment on financial regulation.

State-owned and state-controlled financial actors as buyers (SID banka, SDH-held banks, Zavarovalnica Triglav group, DUTB successors, Poštna banka/Pošta Slovenije) were not individually mapped as contracting authorities or utilities-sector buyers.
No verified CPV code list was assembled for this cell (banking 661xxxxx, payment transaction processing, financial IT 72/48 families) against actual Slovenian notice usage.

Below-EU-threshold and 'naročila male vrednosti' (small-value) procurements — where most municipal banking-services and niche compliance-software contracts sit — are covered only by the national portal and ERAR, not by TED.

Pre-notice planning signals — 'predhodno informativno obvestilo' (prior information notices), načrt javnih naročil (annual procurement plans published by buyers), and budget documents (proračun, finančni načrt Banke Slovenije) — were not collected.
English-language coverage of Slovenian notices is thin outside TED; national-portal content is Slovenian-only.

Non-central-bank supervisory and infrastructure buyers relevant to banking/payments — ATVP (securities), AZN (insurance), Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja (FIU), AJPES, FURS — were not confirmed as tracked contracting authorities.

Only NLB and Bankart are well covered on the supplier side. NKBM/OTP banka, SKB (OTP), Addiko Bank, Gorenjska banka (AIK), Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, Sparkasse, Delavska hranilnica and Deželna banka Slovenije have no vendor-announcement trail collected yet.

Regtech proper - regulatory reporting (AnaCredit, COREP/FINREP, ESG/CSRD reporting), sanctions screening, fraud/PSD3, and instant-payments VoP (Verification of Payee, October 2025 deadline) - has no confirmed SI vendor source yet.

Indirect reveal channels that are usually richer than press releases for private banks were not exploited: vendor job postings, bank job postings naming platforms, LinkedIn vendor case posts, GitHub/tech-blog traces, and bank annual reports' outsourcing/ICT third-party disclosures (now mandatory under DORA's register of information).
None of the listed URLs were fetched or liveness-tested in this pass; several are section/index URLs constructed from observed article URLs rather than directly observed index pages.
